description: Matches the Slayer boss and its cave krakens by exact name rather than a kraken substring, because the Ranged damage division to a seventh and the immunity to melee belong to those monsters, while the Armoured kraken and Pygmy kraken carry neither.

quotes: deals 1/7th of its normal damage
The Kraken cannot be reached with Melee weapons, and is additionally entirely immune to melee attacks
If you rolled 0 damage, it stays as 0. If you rolled >=1 damage, it's divided by 7, with a floor of 1. Accuracy is not affected.

description: Salarin the twisted takes fixed damage from spells, always 9, 10, 11 or 12, whatever the caster's magic damage.

quotes: the spells will always deal 9, 10, 11, or 12 damage

description: Matches revenants by name substring, since every revenant carries the word, so the amulet of avarice's 20% accuracy and damage increase can be applied to them.

quotes: has an additional 20% increase in accuracy and damage when fighting revenants

description: Matches the Corporeal Beast, which halves damage from any weapon that is not a Corpbane weapon used on the stab attack style. Matched on the exact name so no other monster picks up the reduction.

quotes: The Corporeal Beast has a 50% damage reduction against any weapon that is not a Corpbane weapon on stab attack style.

description: Matches zogres, skogres and Slash Bash, which are almost immune to ordinary weapons: accuracy is unchanged but damage is cut by 75%.

quotes: Zogres are almost immune to normal weapons (you will hit just as often, but damage is reduced by 75%).

description: Matches Zulrah, the one monster that needs halberd reach for a reason other than flight: it sits out of melee range in the water and only halberds can reach it. Other airborne creatures carry the Flying attribute instead, so this family stays a single name rather than a list that could miss one.

quotes: It cannot be reached with melee (with the exception of halberds).

description: Matches the airborne targets whose own articles still except salamanders as well as halberds, rather than the halberd-only rule the Flying attribute otherwise carries: aviansies, Kree'arra and his three bodyguards. Left out on purpose are the Armadylean guard, which an update made vulnerable to halberd melee alone in the elite clue fight, and the reanimated aviansie, Dawn and Vespula, whose articles name only halberds.

quotes: As they are airborne, they are immune to being directly targeted by melee attacks except for salamanders and halberds
he and his bodyguards cannot be attacked with Melee, except when using Halberds or Salamanders
Armadylean guards fought while completing elite clue scrolls are now only vulnerable to halberd melee weapons.

description: Matches Zulrah, whose damage is capped at 50 per hitsplat, any larger hit being replaced by a roll of 45 to 50.

quotes: Damage at Zulrah is capped at 50, with any hits greater than this amount dealing 45-50 damage instead.

description: Matches the Nylocas Ischyros, the melee form of the Theatre of Blood spiders, which takes damage from melee only and is immune to the other two styles.

quotes: Each spider is immune to damage outside of their combat style - ranged must be used against the Toxobolos, magic against the Hagios, and melee against the Ischyros.

description: Matches the Nylocas Toxobolos, the ranged form of the Theatre of Blood spiders, which takes damage from Ranged only and is immune to the other two styles.

quotes: Each spider is immune to damage outside of their combat style - ranged must be used against the Toxobolos, magic against the Hagios, and melee against the Ischyros.

description: Matches the Nylocas Hagios, the magic form of the Theatre of Blood spiders, which takes damage from Magic only and is immune to the other two styles.

quotes: Each spider is immune to damage outside of their combat style - ranged must be used against the Toxobolos, magic against the Hagios, and melee against the Ischyros.

description: Matches the white, melee form of the Nylocas Prinkipas in Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode, which only melee can damage. Keyed by the two NPC ids the article's infobox gives for that form, because all three forms share one name.

quotes: with their active combat style and weakness changing according to the colour of their carapace: blue for magic, green for ranged and white for melee

description: Matches the green, ranged form of the Nylocas Prinkipas, which only Ranged can damage. Keyed by the NPC id the infobox gives for that form.

quotes: with their active combat style and weakness changing according to the colour of their carapace: blue for magic, green for ranged and white for melee

description: Matches the blue, magic form of the Nylocas Prinkipas, which only Magic can damage. Keyed by the NPC id the infobox gives for that form.

quotes: with their active combat style and weakness changing according to the colour of their carapace: blue for magic, green for ranged and white for melee

description: Matches the Fragment of Seren, which discards the damage a hit rolled and substitutes a number from 22 to 24.

quotes: ignoring whatever damage you rolled, and simply picking a number 22-24

description: Matches Verzik Vitur's first phase, where melee is capped at 10 damage per hitsplat and Ranged or Magic at 3. Keyed by the entry, normal and hard mode phase-one ids from the article's infobox, because all nine are simply called Verzik Vitur in the bundled bestiary; the name half only fires for a source that does disambiguate the phase.

quotes: Ranged/mage is capped at 3 and melee is capped at 10 damage per hitsplat.

description: Matches the Hueycoatl's tail and its broken form, whose damage is capped at 4, or 9 when the player's crush attack bonus is their highest. Keyed by the two ids from the article's infobox, with a name fallback because some sources carry the body part in a page version rather than in the name; without it the cap would apply to the whole fight or to none of it.

quotes: The tail is subject to a damage cap of 4 or 9, depending on whether the player's crush attack bonus is their highest

description: Matches the totems charged during The Nightmare, which take double damage from magic. Matched on the exact name because the wiki page is simply Totem and the only other totem-named monster, the healing totem, is a different exact name.

quotes: The totems take 2x damage when attacked with magic.

description: Matches Tekton, who is immune to Ranged and takes 80% reduced damage from Magic, stated with no carve-out for his enraged state. Keyed by id as well as by name because the enraged rows are named Tekton (enraged) and share only the page name, which the matcher never reads.

quotes: Tekton is immune to Range and takes 80% reduced Magic damage

description: Matches the Great Olm's head in normal and Challenge Mode, which mitigates 66% of the damage from every style but Ranged. Keyed by the ids from the article's infobox because all the parts share the name Great Olm, the wiki keeping the part in a page version the monster database does not carry.

quotes: The head has 66% damage mitigation from all non-range attacks, and will heal itself if hit outside of Olm's final phase. Olm's right hand (also called mage hand) has 66% damage mitigation from all non-mage attacks. Olm's left hand (also called melee hand) has 66% damage mitigation from non-melee attacks.

description: Matches the Great Olm's left claw, the melee hand, in normal and Challenge Mode, which mitigates 66% of the damage from every style but melee. Keyed by id for the same reason as the head: all the parts share one name.

quotes: The head has 66% damage mitigation from all non-range attacks, and will heal itself if hit outside of Olm's final phase. Olm's right hand (also called mage hand) has 66% damage mitigation from all non-mage attacks. Olm's left hand (also called melee hand) has 66% damage mitigation from non-melee attacks.

description: Matches the Great Olm's right claw, the mage hand, in normal and Challenge Mode, which mitigates 66% of the damage from every style but Magic. Keyed by id for the same reason as the head: all the parts share one name.

quotes: The head has 66% damage mitigation from all non-range attacks, and will heal itself if hit outside of Olm's final phase. Olm's right hand (also called mage hand) has 66% damage mitigation from all non-mage attacks. Olm's left hand (also called melee hand) has 66% damage mitigation from non-melee attacks.

description: Matches the Tombs of Amascut roster by NPC id: Akkha and his shadows, Ba-Ba, Kephri shielded and unshielded with her overlords, Zebak, the obelisk, the Wardens' second phase, ejected cores and third phase, and the path and room monsters (crocodiles, baboons, scarabs, scarab swarms and eggs). The family exists because Osmumten's fang scopes its independent accuracy re-roll to the raid as a whole rather than to its bosses, so every monster inside the tombs must match.

quotes: Within the raid, this check is performed using the standard mechanics, but is repeated

description: Matches the gemstone crab, whose health bar depletes on a timer rather than from player damage and which ruby bolt (e) procs treat as having a fixed 300 hitpoints.

quotes: The health bar of the crab is not affected by player damage, regardless of how many players are attacking it. Instead, it depletes over time to indicate how long until the crab will burrow to its next location.
Ruby bolt (e) special attacks treat the boss as if it has 300 Hitpoints and deal 60 damage, increased to 66 if using a Zaryte crossbow.

description: Matches the targets no combat DPS figure applies to: Zalcano, who is immune to ordinary combat damage and is instead worn down with imbued tephra and then mined, plus Wintertodt and Tempoross, which carry neither hitpoints nor a combat level on the wiki and so are already dropped by the ingest filter, listed here so the omission reads as deliberate. Left out on purpose are the gemstone crab, whose health bar ignores damage but whose DPS ranking still answers the XP-rate question, Vespula, unkillable but genuinely attackable, and the Phantom Muspah's prayer shield and Duke Sucellus's charge bar, which are non-damage phases of otherwise ordinary targets.

quotes: Being immune to traditional combat damage, players must use their Mining, Smithing, and Runecraft skills to create imbued tephra capable of destroying her stone armour. Once her armour has been destroyed, they must damage her by mining her with a pickaxe.

description: Matches both halves of the Royal Titans duo, Eldric the Ice King and Branda the Fire Queen, which share the encounter's mechanics, so both ids carry them.

quotes: The Royal Titans are a boss encounter consisting of the two giants Eldric the Ice King and Branda the Fire Queen.

description: Matches the glowing crystals in Vasa Nistirio's room, which are immune to Ranged and take a third of the damage from Magic. Keyed by the id from the article's infobox, with the name kept as a fallback.

quotes: They are weak to stab attacks, immune to ranged damage (including the ranged thrall), and take 1/3rd damage from magic attacks.

description: Matches the Alchemical Hydra, which starts each phase with a 75% damage reduction that is removed by luring it over the matching chemical vent. Every phase shares the one name, since the wiki keeps the serpentine, fire, electric and extinguished forms in a page version the database does not carry, which is fine here because the resistance is a player-stated option rather than something the engine infers per phase.

quotes: At the start of each phase, it has a 75% damage reduction, which can be removed if it is lured over a vent on the floor which spews chemical liquid.

description: Matches Kamil, who is immune to every kind of magic damage and effect except fire spells. The Nightmare Zone hard-mode row is listed by id because it is named "Kamil (hard)", which the exact-name match cannot reach; the normal-mode row carries the bare name and is matched by it.

quotes: Kamil is weak to fire spells, but is immune to all other magic damage and effects

description: Matches Fareed, who has very high melee defence and can otherwise only be damaged by water spells or a ranged weapon. The Nightmare Zone hard-mode row is listed by id because it is named "Fareed (hard)", which the exact-name match cannot reach; the normal-mode row carries the bare name and is matched by it.

quotes: Fareed has high melee Defence, and can only otherwise be damaged with Water spells or any kind of Ranged weapon.

description: Matches Delrith, who takes double damage from every hit while Silverlight is equipped.

quotes: All damage dealt to Delrith is doubled when Silverlight is equipped

description: Surok Magis, in the While Guthix Sleeps fight, can only be damaged by combat spells cast from a spellbook; powered staves and non-magic styles do nothing to him.

quotes: Surok is notably immune to damage from powered staves, thus the player must use combat spells in order to damage him.

description: Slagilith takes damage reduced to a third from anything that is not a pickaxe. The Nightmare Zone copy carries the same rule with no split between normal and hard mode, so the hard-mode id is matched by the id arm rather than by name. Mod Ash puts the survivor at 33%, which settles the article split between the main page's 67% reduction and the Nightmare Zone page's 66%.

quotes: will reduce your damage by 67% if a pickaxe is not equipped
Damage from non-pickaxe weapons is reduced by 66%.

The Slagilith is a much simpler one than the CoX guardians. It just reduces the damage to 33% if the attacker isn't wielding a pickaxe. There's no scaling for level. Earth elementals don't seem to have any special pickaxe code at all, other than waking them up.

description: The Abyssal Sire's four respiratory systems, the first-phase targets. They share a single name and differ only by id, so matching on the name covers all four at once.

quotes: In the first phase players must kill the Sire's four respiratory systems in the corners of the room

description: Skotizo takes reduced damage while his awakened altars are active: each active altar cuts damage by 25%, up to a total of 100%, or by 15% up to 60% while Arclight or Emberlight is equipped.

quotes: These altars reduce all damage inflicted on Skotizo while they are active. If Arclight or Emberlight is equipped, each altar reduces damage by 15% up to a maximum of 60%. Otherwise, with other weapons, it's 25% each up to a maximum of 100%.

description: Dusk, the second Grotesque Guardian, can only be harmed by melee; Magic and Ranged attacks do nothing. Dawn carries no such rule. Both of Dusk's forms are listed by id, with the unambiguous name as a fallback.

quotes: Dusk is immune to Magic and Ranged attacks; only melee attacks will harm it.

description: Duke Sucellus resists demonbane weapons, keeping 70% of the modifier they would normally apply to damage and accuracy.

quotes: he has 30% demonbane resistance. This means an emberlight would only have 49% increased damage and accuracy against him rather than 70%.

description: Yama amplifies demonbane weapons, applying 120% of their usual damage and accuracy modifier.

quotes: all demonbane modifiers are increased by 20%

description: Void flares take double the usual demonbane modifier, applying 200% of a demonbane weapon's damage and accuracy bonus.

quotes: have 200% demonbane vulnerability

description: The ice demon in the Chambers of Xeric reduces all incoming damage by 67% except from fire spells and demonbane weapons, and amplifies demonbane modifiers to 115% of their usual value. Both the regular and Challenge Mode ids are matched.

quotes: all damage dealt to the demon is reduced by 67%, except for fire spells (which deal 250% damage) and demonbane weapons
increased by 15%

description: The three hatched araxyte minions at Araxxor, which are always hit for the player's maximum when attacked with a noxious halberd, a crush weapon, or a heavy Ranged weapon while that style is the player's most accurate. Matched by id because the three carry different names, and the unhatched eggs are excluded because they roll damage normally.

quotes: Players will always max hit when attacking the hatched araxytes with a noxious halberd, crush weapons, or heavy Ranged weapon (such as a crossbow or ballista) if crush or ranged is their highest accuracy style respectively.
attacking the unhatched eggs - does not guarantee a max hit, and rolls damage normally

description: The Guardian statues in the Chambers of Xeric, which can only be damaged by a pickaxe. Normal and Challenge Mode ids are both listed, and the name fallback uses the full disambiguated form so it cannot also match the Ancient Guardian, guardian drakes or the Guardians of Armadyl.

quotes: can only be harmed with pickaxes; all other sources of damage will not count.

description: Broodoo victims cap the player's maximum hit at 3 against conventional attacks. The three colour variants have two ids each.

quotes: They are highly resistant to conventional attack methods (the player's max hit is reduced to 3)

description: The Abyssal Sire while it is transitioning between phases, during which incoming damage is halved. Only the leading id of phases 1 to 3 is listed; the final stage has no transition.

quotes: Damage dealt to the Sire while it is transitioning between phases is reduced by 50%.

description: Tormented demons carry a fire shield that cuts damage from weapons and spells that are neither demonbane nor abyssal by 20%.

quotes: Tormented demons usually have a fire shield that reduces damage done by non-demonbane weapons/spells and non-abyssal weapons by 20%.

description: The Leviathan, whose lure is out of reach of melee attacks. All three encounters are listed: the normal fight, the awakened fight and the quest fight.

quotes: Your melee attacks can't reach the lure!

description: The Royal Titans' own Fire (14150) and Ice (14151) elementals, whose hit chance follows their magic accuracy against the player.

quotes: is equal to their magic accuracy

description: The Hueycoatl's head and tail, which can benefit from the 30% damage buff players gain while the braziers on the seer's pillars are lit. The body is excluded on phase order rather than on any immunity: the body parts are fought in the first phase and the seer only charges the pillars from the second.

quotes: activating a 30% damage bonus for players. This bonus remains in effect as long as the braziers are lit.
While the braziers are lit, players are given a 30% damage buff.
The seer will begin charging the three pillars located west of the head.

description: The Tombs of Amascut wardens in their second phase, where every attack hits regardless of equipment and the player's accuracy bonuses feed damage instead. Only the phase 2 ids are listed, since each phase shares a name but uses a different damage formula.

quotes: the player having 100% accuracy regardless of equipment; however, the damage dealt corresponds to the player's accuracy bonuses

description: Monsters whose Magic defence roll is built from their Defence level rather than their Magic level: Verzik Vitur in every mode and phase, the ice demon, the Fragment of Seren, the Baboon Brawlers and the Prifddinas rabbit.

Magic attacks are effective due to the demon's magic defence being calculated from its Defence level rather than Magic, unlike most monsters.
Unlike most monsters, the Fragment's Magic defence roll is calculated using her Defence level rather than her Magic level.
unlike most monsters, the Magic defence roll of Baboon Brawlers is calculated using their Defence level rather than their Magic level.

quotes: Fire spells will heal them equal to the amount hit.

like in phase 2, will absorb any defence-draining specials used against her
his strength and defence levels scale linearly with his remaining hitpoints
defence-draining weapons are useless (zero Defence reduction)

won't let her Defence stat go below 120

however this will get restored when she enters final phase

description: Groups every Verzik Vitur phase and mode by name, since all nine bestiary rows share that exact name. Broader than verzikPhaseOne, which narrows to a phase by id.

Nezikchened, the demon holy water gains an extra damage bonus against. Keyed by the ids of the three Nezikchened encounters, the Legends' Quest fight and both replays, because ids cannot drift the way a name can.
